problem: The lead says the flip-flop cell is 'also called a latch', but exam trap 1 says 'Do not treat the names as synonyms'. A student reading both will be confused about whether latch and flip-flop are the same thing.
fix: Lead: say the cross-coupled cell is a latch (bistable multivibrator), and that a clocked, edge-triggered version is what most syllabi call a flip-flop. Keep trap 1 as the reminder that a level-triggered latch and an edge-triggered flip-flop behave differently.

problem: The plain SR latch has no clock or enable input, so calling it 'this level-triggered cell' is inaccurate; level triggering only applies once a clock or enable gate is added (Section 2). It also sits oddly next to the sentence 'A clock is not needed for this basic latch.'
fix: Write: 'This cell with no clock is an asynchronous latch; add an enable gate and it becomes level-triggered.'
